narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>The nine centimetre cube fits, because it is the biggest choice and it divides thirty six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Along the twelve centimetre side, one cube fits and a gap is left.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>It must divide all three sides, not only one, so that slip is struck.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows the nine centimetre cube; a row of 9 cm cubes along the 12 cm side leaves a gap of 3 cm that glows red; the slip's bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>To check a cube, divide each box side by the cube side.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For the six centimetre cube, twelve gives two, eighteen gives three and thirty six gives six.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Every answer is whole, so there is no gap. Repeat for the other two cubes.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the check lines 12 / 6 = 2, 18 / 6 = 3, 36 / 6 = 6 appear with ticks; the words repeat for each cube side appear

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip says the nine centimetre cube fits because it is the biggest choice that divides thirty six. Nine does not divide twelve, so a gap is left along the length.
